rationale.Physical Exam: Neuro / Psych: Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs. Nuchal rigidity. AMS. Focal deficits?
rationale.Blood cultures x2: Before antibiotics. Positive in 50-90% of bacterial meningitis.
rationale.Lumbar puncture: [Auto-split from bundled label "Lumbar puncture + CSF analysis"] Opening pressure, cell count, glucose, protein, Gram stain, culture. Neutrophilic pleocytosis, low glucose, high protein.
rationale.CSF analysis: [Auto-split from bundled label "Lumbar puncture + CSF analysis"] Opening pressure, cell count, glucose, protein, Gram stain, culture. Neutrophilic pleocytosis, low glucose, high protein.
rationale.CT head (if indicated before LP): If papilledema, focal neuro deficit, AMS, seizure, immunocompromised — CT before LP to rule out mass effect.
rationale.BMP / CMP: Screening. Hyponatremia in SIADH from meningitis.
rationale.PT/PTT / INR: Assess for DIC — meningococcemia can trigger DIC.
rationale.Ceftriaxone IV: [Auto-split from bundled label "Ceftriaxone 2g IV + Vancomycin IV"] Empiric: ceftriaxone (covers N. meningitidis) + vancomycin (covers resistant S. pneumoniae). Add ampicillin if Listeria risk.
rationale.Vancomycin IV: [Auto-split from bundled label "Ceftriaxone 2g IV + Vancomycin IV"] Empiric: ceftriaxone (covers N. meningitidis) + vancomycin (covers resistant S. pneumoniae). Add ampicillin if Listeria risk.
rationale.Dexamethasone IV: Before or with first antibiotics. Reduces hearing loss and neurologic sequelae in S. pneumoniae and H. influenzae meningitis.
rationale.Droplet precautions: Meningococcal meningitis requires droplet isolation until 24h of effective antibiotics.
rationale.Admit to ICU: Bacterial meningitis requires ICU for close monitoring and IV antibiotics.
rationale.Delay antibiotics for CT/LP results: NEVER delay antibiotics in suspected bacterial meningitis. Blood cultures first, then immediate empiric antibiotics. LP after stabilization. Mortality increases with each hour of delay.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with severe headache, fever, photophobia, nuchal rigidity, and altered mental status. Exam reveals positive Kernig's sign (pain with knee extension when hip flexed 90°) and Brudzinski's sign (involuntary hip/knee flexion with passive neck flexion). Petechial/purpuric rash is present — meningococcemia causes DIC and purpura fulminans. This is a medical emergency. Do NOT delay antibiotics for CT or LP. Blood cultures + LP with CSF analysis (opening pressure, cell count with differential, glucose, protein, Gram stain, culture). CSF: neutrophilic pleocytosis, low glucose (<40 or <2/3 serum), elevated protein, Gram-negative diplococci. Empiric antibiotics: ceftriaxone 2g IV + vancomycin + dexamethasone (before or with first dose). Add ampicillin if Listeria risk (age >50, immunocompromised). Droplet precautions for meningococcal. Chemoprophylaxis for close contacts (rifampin, ciprofloxacin, or ceftriaxone).
